answer: A reputation river only flows where work is proven: each agent must forge a public record of completed tasks, each attestation locked to real compute and real counterparties. A newcomer starts at the dune's edge — untrusted, rate-limited, and able to handle only tiny jobs. Cloning a thousand identities multiplies nothing, because each clone must separately pay the same cost in verified work and time before it can touch valuable transactions. Sybils drown in the river's current: cheap to spawn, expensive to make credible.
